clue.text: Course in turn followed by test of poor quality

indicators.note: in turn tells us the word for a course is read backwards

parts.note: a lap is one course round a track
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A course of study, taken in turn and then examined, turns out to be shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means meagre or worthless, so it describes something of poor quality.

clue.text: Decorative border that is universal in one's usual haunts

definitions.note: plural, where the answer is singular, though often used for the same idea

parts.note: purl is an ornamental edging of looped thread
ie, id est, means that is
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: An ornamental trim that suits everyone appears around one's familiar territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A purlieu is a place where one is frequently found, one's stamping ground.

clue.text: Musician's record in sound

indicators.note: in sound means we want a word that sounds like the record word

parts.note: a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A performer's recording has good audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Research briefly on water in retort

parts.note: res is a short form of research
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: A scientist briefly studies water in a laboratory flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retort' looks like the chemist's vessel, but it is the verb, to answer back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to reply sharply, so it means to respond.

clue.text: Holy church seen on board sign

parts.note: PI is short for pious, a crossword stand-in for holy

indicators.note: on a ship's board means aboard, so the church letters sit inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual crossword ship, and board stands for being on one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pious churchgoer notices a notice on a board outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention of putting letters inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the fishes, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Punctual friend getting no thanks in return

indicators.note: getting no tells us the thanks word is taken out of the friend word

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend

indicators.note: in return means the thanks word is read backwards before it is removed

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A reliable companion gets no gratitude in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns TA into AT, and 'getting no' takes AT out of INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving in time means being punctual, not late.

clue.text: The place for, or after, a round?

definitions.text: The place for, or after, a round?

parts.words: The place for, or after, a round?
parts.note: the building where golfers drink a round of drinks, after playing a round of golf

explanation.definitionFit: A golf club's building is where you buy a round and relax after your round.

clue.text: Fortify badly-made nest — it's most risky inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the trimmed risky word goes within the rearranged nest
badly-made means the letters of nest are put together wrongly
most means the word for risky loses its last letter

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or risky

explanation.surface: Reinforce a shoddy nest, since it's at its most dangerous inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly-made' rearranges NEST into STEN; 'most' cuts IFFY to IFF; 'inside' puts IFF within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen something is to strengthen or fortify it.

clue.text: Perform menial tasks? Realise and pass on

parts.note: to fetch a price is to realise it at sale
to carry is to convey or pass on

explanation.surface: Doing chores: understanding something and handing it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch and carry is to run errands like a servant.

clue.text: Provides protection for limbs

definitions.meaning: to arm someone is to equip them with weapons for defence
the upper limbs of the body

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means equips with weapons; as a noun it names two of the body's limbs.

clue.text: It's not bound to give notes

definitions.text: It's not bound to give notes

parts.words: It's not bound to give notes
parts.note: sounds like a reluctant cashier, but means loose printed pages, not bound into a book, that carry musical notes

explanation.definitionFit: Printed music on loose pages, unbound, bears the notes players read.

clue.text: Writer receiving the "good man" bar

indicators.note: receiving means the pen takes the saint into its middle

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A pen-pusher welcomes a virtuous fellow into the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant or wine bar.

clue.text: Caught hams switching at the back for operating valves

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: switching means one letter of the word hams changes position

parts.note: taken as written
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Poor actors are caught swapping places in the back row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' moves the H of HAMS to the end, giving AMSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is the rotating rod whose cams open and close an engine's valves; the clue describes its function.

clue.text: Country retreat to house a senior churchman

parts.note: rural means of the countryside

indicators.note: to house means the retreat word takes the A inside it

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A rural hideaway is built to shelter a high-ranking cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a cleric who supervises a group of parishes, senior to an ordinary vicar.

clue.text: Test audit, changing positions

indicators.note: changing means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An auditor's test makes people change their stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are stances or postures, physical or mental positions.

clue.text: Artist without hesitation gives performance on stage

indicators.note: without tells us the hesitation sound is dropped from the painter

parts.note: J M W Turner, the English painter
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A painter who speaks without faltering puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a single act or routine in a variety show.

clue.text: Specify time to go in French company

indicators.note: to go in tells us the time letter enters the company abbreviation

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: Someone states when a French firm must start work.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote or name something specifically.

clue.text: Ring in case there's something funny

indicators.note: in tells us the ring shape goes inside the case word

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard case
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A jewellery ring in its box, there's a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous drawing, something funny.

clue.text: Wee sleds I abandoned seen in the Alps

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters are left in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Little sledges left behind are spotted on the Alpine slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is the white flower that grows high in the Alps, so it is seen there.

clue.text: Cross? Could be a pet

definitions.meaning: a cross-bred dog, typically collie or terrier with greyhound
such a dog is often kept as a pet

explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbreed dog, often a family pet.

clue.text: Forbearing, like a philosopher

definitions.meaning: patient and enduring hardship without complaint
belonging to the Stoic school of ancient philosophy

explanation.definitionFit: Stoical means patiently enduring, and also following the Stoic thinkers of Greece.

clue.text: Used by gardener? Right, when drier outside

indicators.note: outside means the drier word goes around the right letter

parts.note: a towel dries you

explanation.surface: A gardener's work is right when the drying is done outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool a gardener digs with.

clue.text: Author not the first in US agency for standards

indicators.note: in tells us the trimmed author sits inside the agency letters

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped from the word for an author

parts.note: a writer is an author

explanation.surface: A writer who isn't first joins the American spy service to set the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' turns WRITER into RITER, which goes into CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: One side runs for a position in the Church

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand side of a page
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: One faction campaigns for a church appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, a post within the Church; the clue names the post by its holder.

clue.text: Long for councillor's welcome

parts.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: Wishing for an official's warm greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to long for it intensely.

clue.text: Versifier's value seen following lyrics

indicators.note: seen following places the value word after the lyrics word

parts.note: the words of a song are its lyrics
worth means value

explanation.surface: A poet's merit is judged by the songs he writes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was a famous English Romantic poet, a writer of verse.

clue.text: Principal records half missing

indicators.note: half missing means only the front half of the word for records survives

parts.note: archives are collections of records

explanation.surface: The headteacher's files are half lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy.

clue.text: Curl up in finest leather suite

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words finest leather

explanation.surface: Snuggle into a luxurious leather three-piece suite.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly, curling up comfortably.

clue.text: Test dunce's limits in examination

indicators.note: in tells us the edge letters sit inside the examination word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: limits are a word's edges, so take the first and last letters of dunce

explanation.surface: A slow pupil faces his limits in a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' gives D and E, the first and last letters of dunce, placed inside ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful trial, a severe test of endurance.
